title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic high-entropy alloy composed of Tb, Hf, Zr, Ti and V (best guess)
recollection.intervention: Arc-melting of the constituent elements followed by homogenizing anneal at 1200 °C for 48 h and quenching (best guess)
recollection.structure: Single-phase body‐centred cubic (BCC) solid solution with lattice parameter ≈3.35 Å (best guess)
recollection.mechanism: Conventional electron–phonon coupling consistent with BCS theory, enhanced by atomic‐level lattice distortion (best guess)
recollection.results: Onset superconducting transition at Tc ≈4.8 K, upper critical field μ0Hc2(0) ≈2.1 T, critical current density Jc ≈1×10^5 A/cm2 at 2 K (best guess)

score.note: It correctly recalls arc melting, a bcc structure, and a Tc near 4.7 K. However, it invents annealing/quenching, misstates the composition and single-phase character, misses the Tb/Tb2O3 precipitates and comparative Tb-addition design, gives an unsupported mechanism, and substantially underestimates Hc2 while inventing a Jc value.
